sentences.text: For Appellant : Mrs. D.Jeevitha  Respondents 3 & 12 : Mr.R.Neethi Perumal  For Respondents 1, 2, 4 to 11 : Notice not ready  JUDGEMENT

This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is preferred by the claimant, aggrieved by the award passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal cum Special Subordinate Court, Erode, in M.C.O.P.No.577 of 2018 (hereinafter, referred to as 'the Tribunal') dated 15.09.2023.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal cum Special Subordinate Court, Erode
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 2

. On 03.08.2017, at 7.45 p.m. when the claimant was travelling in Fiesta Car,bearing Regn.No.59 AW 6689, which was driven by the first respondent on Kovai to Trichy road from east to west direction, in a rash and negligent manner, the first respondent came to the wrong side of the road and dashed against one car, bear Regn.No.tn 47 AE 4262, which came from opposite direction,
which ultimately resulted in dashing against one car followed by another succeeding cars, which came behind the car bearing Regn.No.tn 47 AE 4262.
In the said accident, the claimant has sustained bone fracture and grievous injuries all over the body and hence, he claimed a sum of Rs.25,00,000/- as compensation.

3. The Tribunal, on consideration of oral and documentary evidence held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligence on the part of the first respondent, who drove the Fiesta Car, bearing Regn.No.TN 59 AW 6689, and hence, directed the respondents 3 and 12/New India Assurance Company to pay a compensation of Rs.6,53,000/- to the claimant together with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a. from the date of filing of the Petition and till the date of deposit and dismissed the claim in respect of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis respondents 4 to 11.

The break up details of the award passed by the Tribunal under various is as follows:-

4.
Aggrieved over the award passed by the Tribunal, the appellant/claimant has filed the present appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.

Since the present Appeal is filed only questioning the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, it is not necessary for this Court to traverse into the other aspects of the award passed by the Tribunal.

6. Mrs. D.Jeevitha, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant would submit that due to the accident, the appellant/claimant sustained severe bone fracture and grievous injuries; that the Medical Board issued a Disability Certificate, which has been marked as Ex.C.1, wherein, the disability was assessed as partial permanent disability at 25%; that, the Tribunal, while determining compensation under the head, 'Disability' by adopting percentage method, fixed only a sum of Rs.5,000/- towards per percentage of disability, which has resulted in awarding an inadequate compensation of Rs.1,25,000/- under the said head.

Further, the learned counsel in support of her contention relied on a decision rendered by the Hon'ble Division Bench of this Court in Future General India Insurance Comp. Ltd., Vs. 1. Manivannan and two others, dated 15.06.2022, wherein,
a sum of Rs.7,000/- is fixed towards per percentage of disability.

entities.text: Future General India Insurance Comp. Ltd., Vs. 1. Manivannan and two others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the learned counsel prayed to re-determine the compensation https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis awarded by the Tribunal towards Disability by fixing a sum of Rs.7,000/- towards per percentage of disability.

6.1 The learned counsel would also submit that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads, more particularly, i) Attender Charges and Extra Nourishment is also not adequate,
and sought for proper enhancement of the compensation amount.

7. Per contra, Mr.R.Neethi Perumal, learned counsel for the respondents 3 and 13, viz., New India Assurance Co. Ltd., would submit that the appellant/claimant is only a ITI Student, and at the time of the accident, he was aged about 19 years, and the Tribunal taking into consideration of the same awarded compensation under various heads, which is just and fair and the same may be confirmed.
However, he averred the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards Medical Expenses at a sum of Rs.4,38,000/- is on the higher side and the same may be appropriately reduced.

sentences.text: I have given due consideration to the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the appellant/claimant and learned counsel for the respondents 3 and 12 and perused the materials available on record.

9. Thus, this Court taking into consideration of the submission made by both sides and in the light of the decision relied on by the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant, is inclined to re-determine the compensation towards 'Loss of Earning Power due to Disability'', by fixing a sum of Rs.7,000/- towards per percentage of disability and accordingly, the compensation is re-determined in the following manner:_ Rs.7,000/-Per percentage of Disability x 25 % Disability =
Rs.1,75,000/-
9. 1

Consequently, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head 'Disability' at Rs.1,25,000/- is modified and enhanced to Rs.1,75,000/-
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 9.2
So far as the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the two heads, viz., 'Attender's Charges' at Rs.15,000/- and Extra Nourishment' at Rs.10,000/- is concerned
, this Court feels the same to be on the lower side and hence, the same stands modified and enhanced to Rs.30,000/- and Rs.20,000/- respectively.

9.3 Further, this Court finds that no compensation was awarded by the Tribunal towards 'Future Medical Expenses', and hence, a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under the said head.
9.4

As regards the compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards Medical Expenses at a sum of Rs.4,38,000/-, this Court taking into consideration of the fact that due to the accident, the appellant/claimant sustained severe bone fracture, and head injury with right frontal contusion,
right shaft of femur fracture, infected fracture shaft of femur @ Inic Nail Instto, and that, he was admitted as inpatient in the Hospital at Dr.Muthu's Hospital, Coimbatore and Coimbatore Medical College Hospital, Coimbatore for more than two weeks coupled with the further that he also https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis underwent treatment at GH Hospital for a period of 75 days, is of the view that the compensation awarded under the said head is just and fair and the same stands confirmed.
9.5 Insofar as the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under all other heads are concerned, this Court finds the same to be just and proper and is hereby confirmed.

9.6 Thus, the total compensation payable to the appellant/claimant under various Heads is as hereunder:-

Extra Nourishment Rs. 2 R.Shankar vs C.Manojkumar on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106303960/

Consequently, the total compensation amount of Rs.6,53,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is hereby modified and enhanced to Rs.7,68,000/- which shall carry interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit.

11. In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal filed by the appellant/claimant is partly allowed on the following terms:-
(i) The respondents 3 and 12, viz., New India Assurance Co. Ltd., is directed to deposit the entire amount awarded by this Court equally along with interest at the rate of 7.5 % p.a. and costs before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment, after deducting the amount already deposited, if any.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

(ii) On such deposit being made by the respondent/Assurance Company, the Tribunal shall transfer the amount directly to the appellant's/ claimant's respective bank account through RTGS within a period of three weeks thereon.
(iii) The appellant/claimant is entitled to withdraw the entire award amount, less the amount already withdrawn, if any, by making necessary application before the Tribunal.
iv) The appellant/claimant is directed to pay the court fee for the enhanced compensation, if any.
v) There shall be no order as to costs.
